Motivation is such a bizzare concept, I don't really think it exists. I think it's really a mixed bag of emotions like compulsion, coercion, guilt, greed, envy, shame etc.

What you are doing is a natural part of periodization. Essentially, it's a program where you work out for 10-12 weeks, then take 1-2 weeks off. It allows your body to recover. You can't be at peak condition 24/7/365. I do a number of cycles a year. I pick key dates I want to be in top condition for, and train to those dates.

As Erroneous says, you just need to find a new goal. Sometimes I binge eat on my rest week or two just so I'll have some kind of goal at the gym. Usually takes about a week to make any gained fat disappear again.

I'd also suggest creating a completely different workout. Choose entirely different exercises, and build a new routine. When that gets boring, change it up again. Suggestions from my current workout: swimming, rowing, clean and jerks (awesome if you've never tried an olympic lift), front squats, lunges, sumo deadlifts.

Pick something that sounds fun.

The game seemed a bit grindy and didn't really catch my eye the way other games have, so I quit. With it being F2P I might give it a go again, but was wondering what I've missed.
Haven't played Aion since launch, any big changes that might bring me back?

Yes actually quite a bit has changed!

Tons of quality of life upgrades to every aspect of the game since launch. New classes (Aethertechs and gunners are pretty cool), pets, mounts, housing, skills, types of gear enhancements , upgraded maps and quest information and so on.

They have addressed the grind issue quite a bit. There is now a "Fast-Track" server anyone can switch to for most of the way to level 50, which also doesn't have active world PvP so you can focus on leveling. There are also lots of XP boosting items you can obtain, as well as the rechargeable Energy of Repose you get while logged out of the game. If you log out in a studio or house the recharging rate increases.

The story has advanced a bit now, I don't know how far you got into that, but Atreia just experienced a cataclysm event in the most recent patch. Some zones and even skills were destroyed, and some new areas have been revealed. The new high level zones have Rifts, so world PvP is a thing again. It's an interesting time. You should definitely check it out, I'm sure I leaving something out.

I have actually started playing again until I can get all my friends on Wildstar when it goes f2p. I am really enjoying what little I have played of it.

Also, YAY for there being a subverse for it!

Massive differences, but still very much the same game. For a start there's a lot more content, although what you get depends on whether you're NA or EU. It's also way less grindy, particularly on NA as their fast rookie server has extra XP gain.

If you want to get a better idea it's worth reading through the patch notes about things relating to your class, and you'll find the map has changed a fair bit, although all the inner world stuff is much the same.

Level cap is now 65, there's a wealth of endgame content, and PvP gear is way easier to get than in 1.0 so you can get into it within a month and be reasonably well geared in 2 if you work at it.
